event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: EW’s 2024 filing characterizes COVID-19 as both an historic shock and a still-unfolding source of operational strain.  The company discloses that the pandemic continues to suppress procedure volumes, strain hospital budgets, tighten labour availability and unsettle supply chains—factors that directly influence its ability to manufacture, ship and sell cardiovascular devices.  Several statements identify concrete, current-year impacts (e.g., 2023 staffing shortages in the U.S. and Europe, lingering demand volatility in Japan) and forecast that these pressures will persist as the healthcare ecosystem ‘rebalances’ in a post-COVID environment.  Other passages are more generic, positioning pandemics as one of many potential public-health crises.  Taken together, the risk is partially realised (actual 2023 hits) and partially prospective (expected further headwinds).  Because the pandemic began less than four years before the 2024 filing date, the Time Decay Principle permits moderately high scores (up to ~7-8) for direct, quantified language, while generic or anticipatory wording warrants mid-level scores (≈3-4).

evidence_list.snippet: We are subject to risks associated with public health crises, particularly with respect to the pressures that such crises create on the hospital systems and supply chains in which we operate.

components.reason: Acknowledges exposure to public-health crises broadly, creating a link to the pandemic theme.
Specifies two concrete operational vectors—hospital systems and supply chains—showing relevance to core business processes.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but specific enough to mention supply-chain and hospital stress; appropriate mid-level weight (4/10) under Time Decay.

evidence_list.snippet: We are subject to risks associated with public health crises, including pandemics and epidemics, such as COVID-19.

components.reason: Explicitly cites COVID-19, directly tying disclosure to the analysed event.
Framed as a general risk statement without detail or quantified impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct reference to COVID-19 but high-level and un-quantified, yielding a modest risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Other public health crises, including any future epidemics or pandemics, are highly uncertain and difficult to predict, and could result in material adverse impacts on our business and financial condition.

components.reason: Warns of potentially ‘material adverse impacts,’ signalling magnitude.
Highlights uncertainty and unpredictability, which heightens perceived risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking and qualitative; signals materiality but remains hypothetical, so risk is moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: While conditions related to the COVID-19 pandemic have improved compared to 2022, we have continued to experience the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2023, particularly in Japan and disruptions related to staffing shortages in the United States and Europe.

components.reason: Confirms ongoing, realised impacts in the latest fiscal year.
Details geographic specificity (Japan, U.S., Europe), underscoring breadth.
Flags staffing shortages—an acute operational constraint.
Notes partial improvement versus prior year, a mitigating signal.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct evidence of current impacts, partially offset by mention of improvement; scores toward the upper-mid range.

evidence_list.snippet: We expect to continue to experience adverse effects related to COVID-19 for some time, particularly as hospital systems continue experiencing budget constraints and staffing shortages, the supply chains continue to adjust to the market, and medical procedure rates and demand for our products continue to fluctuate as the medical system rebalances its infrastructure and resources in a post-COVID-19 market.

components.reason: Projects continued adverse effects, indicating persistence of risk.
Lists specific pressure points: hospital budget constraints and staffing shortages.
Highlights demand volatility for the company’s products—a direct revenue concern.
Contextualises as part of a ‘rebalancing’ post-COVID market, implying gradual normalization (minor mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive, forward-looking description of multiple continuing pain points; warrants a high (but sub-max) score under Time Decay.
